mechanism.base.value: Water is what metal becomes when it stops holding its shape. In the old texts the cold blade gathers dew out of the morning air, and metal melted in enough heat runs like a river, so the child of steel is the stream. What the edge kept hard and silent, the water carries off and says. A spring under a mountain is the ore learning to move.

mechanism.catalyst_turn.value: With too little Water, the blade stays dry: everything you sharpen is kept inside, and nobody gets the use of it. Show one unfinished thing to one person before it is ready.

value.text: Making something for someone is the most natural thing you do. Water runs low in you, so the little that flows goes straight to whoever is nearest. You give it because giving is easy, or because being needed is the proof you have. The price is never learning which.

value_b.text: What lives in you gets out without a fight, and it arrives as care. Water is scarce in you, so expression gets served one plate at a time. You feed people because you enjoy it, or so nothing is left to say about yourself. What goes untold is your own story.

value.text: You say the line that is too good to sit on. Little Water reaches your chart, so what gets out arrives sharp, shaped on the edge first. You aim it at the idea, or at the person holding the idea and call that the same. The person it landed on carries it home.

function.advise_catalyst.value: Keeping it in feels like control, and mostly it is pressure with the lid on. Write a page most mornings and send one a week to somebody who answers. Cook for people once a month and let them watch. Say one thing at the table that you would usually only think. Hum while you do the dishes.

cta_verdict.value: What you say or make comes out with a clean edge already on it, and it gets quoted back to you later more often than you expect.
cta_verdict.value_b: Speaking and making are how the pressure in you leaves, so a week without either shows up in your mood before it shows up anywhere else.
